content:
The divisor count pattern \(14=7\cdot 2\) gives the exponent structure
\[
N=p^6 q
\]
with \(p,q\) distinct primes.

Since \(N<2000\), \(p^6<2000\), so \(p=2\) or \(p=3\).

- If \(p=3\), then \(N=729q\), and \(1000\le 729q<2000\) forces \(q=2\), which does not end in \(1\).
- If \(p=2\), then \(N=64q\). Four-digit and \(<2000\) gives
  \[
  1000\le 64q<2000 \implies q\in\{17,19,23,29,31\}.
  \]
  Only \(q=31\) ends in \(1\).

Thus
\[
N=64\cdot 31=1984.
\]

\[
\boxed{1984}
\]
